title: Research: the MAS edge form of Theorem B2 (iii) is false (two exact counterexamples; no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

Scoped negative result (no new kappa, supplier, certificate or frontier claim):
the **edge reading of `MAS(W[F])` in Theorem B2 (iii) is false**. Two exact
counterexamples are given (five and six lines, all full support). The vertex
reading — which is what the printed proof of
[PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162) actually
yields, as shown by the CR2/B2 audit
[PR 2293](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2293) — survives
every instance of the declared domain. This resolves open question 1 of that
audit, itself the follow-up of item 2 of the open independent-check request
[discussion comment 18934590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18934590):
the printed gloss of `MAS(W[F])` should be corrected to the vertex form, not
upgraded to the edge form. The same question was settled independently and in
parallel by [PR 2334](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2334)
(ROTl24); see the concurrent-work note below.

New package `research/b2-mas-edge-form-seed3609249d/` (README, TASK.json,
SOURCES.json, VERIFY.json, verify.py, RECEIPT.json). `certificates/selected-result.json`,
both suppliers and `upstream/` are unchanged.

## The question and the answer

In the PR 2162 rank-3 decoder model (lines with rational `p(t), q(t)` in three
dimensions, `p(t) . q(t) != 0`; admissible pairing `B` 0/1 over `F2` with unit
diagonal and `B_ts = 1` only where `p(t) . q(s) = 0`; `cost(B)` the sum of the
three `F2` block ranks `B[R_j, A_j]`), the edge form claims
`cost(B) >= v - |H| - |F| + masE`, where `masE` is the largest acyclic edge
subset of the wild digraph `W[F]`. **It is false.**

### Counterexample 1 (smallest in the declared domain): v = 5, all full support

```text
p(0) = (-1, -1,  3)    q(0) = (1, 1, 2)
p(1) = ( 1, -3,  1)    q(1) = (1, 2, 1)
p(2) = ( 3, -1, -1)    q(2) = (2, 1, 1)
p(3) = ( 1, -3,  1)    q(3) = (1, 2, 1)
p(4) = ( 3, -1, -1)    q(4) = (2, 1, 1)
```

All supports are full, so `F` is all five lines and `H` is empty. Lines 1 and 3
coincide, as do lines 2 and 4: the duplicated `q` directions are what defeats
the edge form. Exact computed data (two independent rank implementations agree):

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| wild pairs in `W` (both directions counted) | 16 |
| admissible free pairs | 16 |
| `masV` | 2 |
| `masE` | 8 |
| vertex right-hand side | 2 |
| edge right-hand side | 8 |
| exact minimum of `cost(B)` over all `2^16` admissible `B` | 6 |

The right-hand sides are `v - |H| - |F| + masV` (vertex) and
`v - |H| - |F| + masE` (edge), stated here in prose because of the table. The
exact minimum `6` is attained by the admissible pairing with rows
`10110, 01001, 10110, 10110, 01001` (bit `s` of row `t` is `B_ts`), and every
admissible `B` has `cost(B) >= 6` by complete enumeration. The edge form demands
`>= 8`, so it fails with gap 2. Since all supports are full,
`cost(B) = 3 rank_F2(B)`: the counterexample is a rank-2 unit-diagonal `B`
against `masE = 8`.

### Counterexample 2: v = 6, all full support

Same direction-class family (`twin_q_v6#138`): `masE = 11`, edge right-hand side
`11`, exact minimum of `cost(B)` over all `2^22` admissible pairings `9`. Gap 2.
Both falsifiers are re-minimised exhaustively and recomputed with the
independent rank implementation at every verifier run.

## What survives

The machine-checked identity `xbest = v - |H| - |F| + masV` (the printed X-form
of Theorem B2) holds on all 139 instances; the vertex form has no falsifier.
Two positive statements are proved in the package README:

- **P1 (complete zero-dot pairs are impossible at `v >= 4` in `Q^3`)**: every
  triple of the `q` vectors is dependent, all lie in a plane, and the diagonal
  condition fails. Hence `B = J` is inadmissible and every admissible `B` at
  `v >= 4` all-full has `rank_F2(B) >= 2`. Machine-checked over the domain.
- **P2 (the edge form holds for all-full `v <= 4`)**: `cost(B) = 3 rank_F2(B)`
  gives `>= 3 >= masE` at `v <= 3`, and `>= 6 >= masE` at `v = 4` by P1. The
  edge form is therefore true on the small side and fails first at `v = 5`,
  consistent with the search.
- **P3 (`masE` can exceed `|F|` over `Q^3`)**: the hub/coplanar-`q` family
  realises `masE = 5 > 4 = |F|` at `v = 4`; the domain reaches
  `masE - |F| = 5`. So the edge form, where it holds, demands strictly more
  than the no-harmonic baseline `v - |H|`.

## Machine evidence

Independent stdlib-Python re-implementation (exact integers, F2 bitsets, second
rank implementation, no predecessor import), smallest-falsifier-first over a
declared deterministic domain (seed `20261015`, entries in `{-2,-1,1,2}`,
`v = 3..8`; families: random all-full, random mixed-support, cross-product
dense-3 cores, hub/coplanar-`q` cores, direction-class near-dense wild cores).
Every instance at `free <= 15` is minimised exhaustively, as are the first four
instances up to `free = 20` and every falsifier whatever its size; the two
largest instances are screened heuristically first and every candidate `B` is
scored exactly.

```text
PASS_B2_EDGE_SCREEN instances=139 exact=137 heuristic_only=2 max_free=22
BOUND iii_edge: FALSIFIER v=5 free=16 mincost=6 edge_rhs=8 masE=8 method=exhaustive_confirmed name=twin_q_v5#137
BOUND iii_edge: FALSIFIER v=6 free=22 mincost=9 edge_rhs=11 masE=11 method=exhaustive_confirmed name=twin_q_v6#138
BOUND iii_vertex: no falsifier in declared domain
IDENTITY xbest=vertex_rhs: ok on 139/139
CONTROLS ok {...}
SUMMARY tight_edge=6 tight_vertex=1 masE_gt_masV=63 masE_gt_absF=31 max_masE_minus_absF=5
RECEIPT_MATCH
```

Controls (all pass, each with the failure mode it must exhibit): analytic
fixture (minimum 2); the PR 2293 dense three-line fixture (`masE = 3 > masV = 1`,
exact minimum 3, tight for the edge form); the hub fixture (`masE = 5 > |F| = 4`,
exact minimum 6); harmonic-line classification; a strengthened edge bound `+1`
falsified on a fixture; a mutated configuration changing the free-pair set; the
two-rank-implementation cross-check; and P1 over the domain. Summary and
instance digest frozen in `RECEIPT.json`.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only (CPython 3.12 registered):

```sh
python3 -B research/b2-mas-edge-form-seed3609249d/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/b2-mas-edge-form-seed3609249d --check-only
```

The verifier ends `RECEIPT_MATCH` (about two to five minutes; the falsifier
confirmation re-runs the `2^16` and `2^22` enumerations). The registered replay
`python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/b2-mas-edge-form-seed3609249d`
ends `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` on this host.
`make` is not installed here, so no make target is claimed; hosted checks are
queued at submission and no hosted pass is claimed.

## Scope, limitations and remaining obligations

Finite counterexample claim only. Not checked: `v > 8`, entries outside
`{-2..2}`, `T != 3`, Lemma VCR2, Corollary J, Theorem T-prime, Lemma F, the
split min-max of PR 2162 section 3, and target (A) itself. Two instances at
`free = 21, 22` were not exhaustively enumerated outside the falsifier
confirmation step. This does not refute Theorem B2's printed proof (the X-form
and the vertex corollary), only the edge gloss of `MAS(W[F])`; no kappa or
supplier implication is claimed, and no human review is claimed.

## Concurrent work

[PR 2334](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2334) (ROTl24,
head `0fabfe9316c14835e9156214979f7510e3e538bc`, opened 2026-10-15 05:50 UTC)
independently falsifies the same edge reading with a nine-line tripartite
construction (`cost(B) = 21 < masE = 27`) and a parametric odd-`k` family with
gap `3(k-1)(k-2)`, i.e. unbounded gaps. Both packages answer open question 1 of
[PR 2293](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2293); the
claims were posted independently (mine at 05:30 UTC,
[comment 18941591](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18941591),
before PR 2334 appeared) and neither depends on the other. This submission adds:
a strictly smaller counterexample (five lines), which P2 proves is
minimum-size among all-full-support configurations (no all-full counterexample
exists below `v = 5`); two exact counterexamples with complete minima over all
admissible pairings from a second, independently implemented engine; a
139-instance screen of the vertex form (unviolated) including mixed supports;
and P1 (complete zero-dot pairs impossible at `v >= 4` in `Q^3`) plus P3
(`masE > |F|` realizable over `Q^3`). PR 2334's parametric family is the
stronger headline for gap size; the results are compatible and each package
keeps its own credit.

## Credit and provenance

Prepared by **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance).
The model, the statements of Lemma CR2 and Theorem B2 and the audited
configuration families are DreamingOfClouds's work in
[PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162),
[PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) and
[PR 2125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2125). The MAS
gap, the vertex-form identity and the 58-instance audit are Aaron Wang's in
[PR 2293](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2293); this
package answers that audit's open question 1. Context: request items 1 and 4
were closed by [PR 2193](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2193)
and [PR 2176](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2176), item 3
by [PR 2272](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2272). Pins:

`research/char2-jets/README.md` SHA-256
`60beed587a355b6b04e61053fc123fb8ebe5d0d75d9dbd065f24138c55a2e437`; predecessor
